items.title: Four candidates for the Wizards’ final roster spot
items.content:
WASHINGTON, DC - FEBRUARY 01: DeMar DeRozan #10 of the Sacramento Kings handles the ball against Anthony Gill #16 of the Washington Wizards during the second half at Capital One Arena on February 1, 2026 in Washington, DC. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images	Preseason hoops begin in less than two months. And the Washington Wizards remain one standard contract short of the NBA limit.

The Wizards currently roster 14 players on standard deals. They have roughly $11.5 million in luxury tax space and own the full non-taxpayer mid-level exception, which is valued at roughly $15 million.

Plenty of time remains between now and when rosters become official on opening night in late October. But as it stands, here are four players Washington could sign to its final roster spot.

The savvy veteran: DeMar DeRozanThe Wizards have held talks with free agent forward DeMar DeRozan in recent weeks, ESPN’s Shams Charania reported. Washington is one of four teams — alongside the Denver Nuggets, Cleveland Cavaliers and Miami Heat — that have expressed interest in the 37-year-old.

The six-time NBA All-Star averaged 18.4 points across 77 games with the Sacramento Kings last season. His 26,711 career points rank 16th on the NBA’s all-time scoring list.

If Washington signs DeRozan, its already crowded rotation would welcome another proven veteran alongside Khris Middleton on the wing. Depth is a good problem to have, but it’s unclear whether DeRozan would immediately be part of the Wizards’ rotation.

Among teams with reported interest, it appears the Wizards could offer the most money. But if DeRozan prefers the destination with the best opportunity to win a championship next season, rival suitors make more sense.

While Washington has expressed interest, this appears a long-shot pairing.

The in-house candidate: Anthony GillSome may view this as an unexciting signing. But Gill provides stability for a team undergoing noteworthy changes — both in personnel and expectations.

The 33-year-old forward is the longest-tenured Wizard. A return would mark his seventh season in Washington, many of those years spent mentoring the team’s young players.

Gill averaged 5.8 points and 2.9 rebounds across 55 appearances last season. He’s likely not the most skilled option, but his relationships within the organization and suitable contributions as a small-ball five could keep him around for another year, especially as the team’s 15th option who’s seldom asked to play meaningful minutes.

Fills a need: Gabe VincentIt’s no secret Washington needs guard depth after trading two guards — D’Angelo Russell and Jaden Hardy — in deals that brought back a forward (Khris Middleton) and center (Deandre Ayton). Recent reports from Hoops Hype’s Michael Scotto confirmed Washington’s interest

items.title: And-Ones: Offseason Rankings, 2027 FAs, Ellis, Smailagic
items.content:
In three separate stories for The Athletic, David Aldridge ranks the offseason moves of each NBA team. The Pelicans (No. 30), Warriors (No. 27) and Knicks (No. 21) are among the teams in Aldridge’s bottom 10, with the Suns (No. 20), Celtics (No. 12) and Lakers (No. 11) falling in the middle tier.

So which teams had the best offseasons? Aldridge believes the Hornets (No. 3), Heat (No. 2) and Sixers (No. 1) deserve kudos for the work they did this summer.

As Aldridge writes, Charlotte received strong return packages when they traded away LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges; Miami acquired two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo; and Philadelphia had a transformative offseason, prompting Aldridge to say new president of basketball operations Mike Gansey should win the Executive of the Year award.

Here’s more from around the basketball world:

Looking ahead to the 2027 offseason, Dan Devine of Yahoo Sports lists his five most interesting potential free agents, starting with Warriors star Jimmy Butler, who is currently recovering from a torn right ACL. Michael Porter Jr. of the Nets and RJ Barrett of the Raptors are among the other players on Devine’s list.
Alcorn State has named former NBA guard Monta Ellis as the new general manager of the men’s basketball program, the school announced in a press release. A Mississippi native who spent 12 years in the NBA after being selected 40th overall in the 2005 draft, Ellis averaged 17.8 points, 4.6 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 833 regular season contests (34.8 minutes per game) with Golden State, Milwaukee, Dallas and Indiana.
Serbian big man Alen Smailagic has signed with the Turkish club Galatasaray, per an announcement from the team. The 39th overall pick of the 2019 draft, Smailagic spent two seasons with Golden State prior to continuing his career overseas. After a three-year run with Partizan Belgrade, the 25-year-old played for Zalgiris Kaunas in 2024/25 and spent last season with Virtus Bologna in Italy, another EuroLeague club.
